title: Relative atomic mass: the average of the isotopes
goal: See how the relative atomic mass of chlorine depends on how abundant each of its two isotopes is.
note: Most elements are a mixture of isotopes. The relative atomic mass is the average of the isotope masses, weighted by the percentage of each isotope in a natural sample.

graphs.title: The relative atomic mass falls as the lighter isotope becomes more abundant.
graphs.label: Relative atomic mass

sentences: Chlorine has two isotopes, chlorine-35 and chlorine-37, and the rest of the sample is chlorine-37.
The relative atomic mass is the average of the two masses, weighted by how abundant each isotope is.

predict.prompt: The lighter isotope of chlorine is more abundant than the heavier one. Will the relative atomic mass be closer to the mass of the lighter or the heavier isotope?
predict.reveal: Set the abundance of chlorine-35 to 75 and compare the relative atomic mass with the two isotope masses.

concept_check.question: What does the relative atomic mass of an element depend on?
options: The masses of its isotopes and how abundant each is
concept_check.explanation: An element is a mixture of isotopes, so its relative atomic mass is the average of their masses weighted by the natural abundance of each.

hints: An element can be a mixture of atoms with different masses.
Which isotope is more abundant? The average leans towards it.
Multiply each mass by its percentage, add them and divide by one hundred.
